summary: Since the city's new transit plan rolled out on September 15th, 2023, a once sleepy neighborhood has seen major changes: electric buses, tram lines, expanded bike lanes, on-demand senior shuttles, free student passes and shared rideshares. Residents of all ages describe benefits including punctuality, independence, safety, cleaner air and more business for local shops. The city has announced further upgrades such as smart traffic management and autonomous vehicles.
one_line: Neighborhood residents describe how the September 2023 city transit plan, with electric buses, trams, bike lanes and shuttles, changed daily life and local businesses.
key_facts: The new city transit plan was rolled out on September 15th, 2023.

The diesel bus fleet was replaced with energy-efficient electric buses; librarian Marjorie Simmons, 58, calls the change "nothing short of revolutionary" and says punctuality gave her 15 extra minutes each morning.
The city council expanded bike lanes in late September 2023; Alex Nguyen, 36, a computer programmer, now rides with his two kids several times a week.
Helen Dorsey, 75, who has arthritis, uses on-demand shuttle services for people with mobility challenges to get to appointments independently.
In October 2023 the 'Students on the Move' initiative began, offering free monthly passes to students in the neighborhood.
Isabella Torres, 18, student council president, created 'Students on the Move' to ease the financial burden on families.
Jenny's Java café has seen more patrons since the tram line was established in October 2023; owner Jenny Park, 43, is considering extending operating hours.
Michael Thompson, 62, community leader, says streets feel safer, air cleaner, and there is a new buzz, with more people chatting in public spaces.
Several rideshare companies introduced shared-ride options in September 2023, meaning less waiting and lower costs.
Gabriela Ruiz, 29, a graphic designer, combines rideshares with public transport but says buses and trams are unbeatable for her daily commute.
Ecologist Luther King, 50, notes reduced carbon emissions and benefits for local flora and fauna.
The city has announced future plans including smart traffic management systems and autonomous vehicles.
